subject: API v1/chat sunsetting — gaps, comms template, and exception request
messages:
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: sam.patel@arcadia-health.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: API v1/chat sunsetting — gaps, comms template, and exception request

Team —

Quick summary: we are starting outreach for the planned sunsetting of the API v1/chat endpoints (internal RFC linked below). Arcadia Health is flagged as a high-risk customer because they use the legacy streaming SDK and have a procurement window that overlaps our target sunset. Sam (cc'd) asked for an exception window and a comms template.

Asks:
- Ben: can you confirm the current committed usage and whether Arcadia is on any support contract that would require a formal extension? I attached a rough impact sheet with customers we think need a one-off migration lane.
- Marissa: what are the minimal compatibility shims we can offer (e.g., a proxy shim or short-term routing to dedicated capacity)? Are there measurable latency/cost implications?
- Markus: ops question — if we grant a 90-day exception for a customer, what telemetry or rollback gates do we require?

Attachments: customer-impact-spreadsheet.xlsx (internal impact by org), comm-template-v1-to-v2.docx (draft for review).

Proposed timeline:
- May 20: confirm list of customers for exception lanes
- May 22: finalize comms template and legal note
- May 25: customer-facing comms go out

Sam — can you confirm whether procurement needs an MSA amendment or a formal addendum to accept an exception? If you prefer, Ben can join a short call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com

Subject: Re: API v1/chat sunsetting — gaps, comms template, and exception request

Thanks Jasmine — quick data points from my side:

- Arcadia Health: ~1.1M tokens/month on v1/chat, streaming SDK usage ~65% of that traffic. They are on a channel partner deal (discounted committed capacity) but not on an enterprise SLA that requires a legal amendment for short exceptions.
- Procurement note: procurement@arcadia-health.com (copied) wants a single-page confirmation they can attach to their internal change request — no full MSA amendment is expected if we keep the exception to 60-90 days.

Proposed customer asks for the template:
- One-paragraph explanation of the deprecation and target cutover date
- Concrete migration steps and a link to a compatibility shim (if we can provide one)
- Point of contact + escalation path (SE + CS + escalation email)

I reviewed the attached spreadsheet and marked Arcadia as medium risk (column H). I'll join the call tomorrow; suggest a 20-min sync with Sam and procurement to lock the language.

—Ben
Ben Carter

Jasmine / Ben — rough technical guidance from Product on what we can safely promise:

1) Compatibility shim: we can ship a lightweight proxy (no model change) that translates streaming frames to the new streaming protocol for up to 60 days with minimal validation. Performance impact: expect an additional 10-20ms p99 per token and ~5% higher infra cost for routed traffic.
2) Longer exceptions (61–90 days): needs a short-term routing policy that pins traffic to dedicated capacity; this requires ops approval and a temporary capacity reserve (we'll need a signed capacity commitment).
3) We cannot promise indeterminate long-term compatibility; mark the customer as "timed exception only" in the comms language.

I updated the comm-template doc with two variants — short exception + routed dedicated lane. See the Google doc link in metadata.

Next steps for us:
- Ben to confirm whether Arcadia can accept the 60-day shim first, or needs longer.
- Jasmine to provide the customer-facing schedule and SE availability for migration assistance.
- Markus to confirm capacity gating and telemetry gates for rollback/termination.

Marissa Cole
Director, Product — Inference Platform
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: sam.patel@arcadia-health.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: API v1/chat sunsetting — gaps, comms template, and exception request

Thanks — good thread.

Decision summary:
- Approve up to 60-day compatibility shims for Arcadia Health without additional capacity commitment.
- For any request between 61–90 days, require a temporary capacity reservation (ops will provision) and a written commit from the customer to migrate within that window.
- Telemetry & rollback gates (must be met for continued exception):
  - Error rate (5xx) remains < 0.5% over rolling 24h
  - Latency p99 increase due to shim remains < 50ms relative to baseline
  - No sustained token-rate spikes > 2x forecast without customer and AE approval

Operational asks:
- Ops: create a short runbook for provisioning the shim route and an automated health-check dashboard.
- SEs/AEs: use the comm-template-v1-to-v2.docx (attached) for customer-facing language; ensure the template includes the clause that exceptions are time-limited and telemetry-gated.
- Legal: if procurement still demands, we can provide a single-page addendum template — Ben, flag if needed and I'll loop legal.

Sam — we'll prepare that single-page confirmation for your procurement team and propose the first customer comms on May 25. Ben will coordinate the 20-min call. If you want a draft before the call, we'll push the template to you today.

Markus Klein
VP, Platform Operations
markus_klein@redwood.com
